title: Book One · Chapter 76: Three Small Stones
story:
Miss Wu puts three small stones on the table.

There are scraps of thick paper too. Short pieces of wood lie beside two empty lids. The stones are clean now. They are smooth enough to hold. Miss Wu does not want stones in anyone's mouth.

“We will not put stones in our mouths,” Leo says.

Miss Wu looks at him.

“Last week someone tasted the paste.”

Leo closes his mouth. Ronan remembers Leo's surprised face from last week. Ronan keeps his smile behind his hand.

Today they will test a small boat with stones. How many stones can it carry? Each group has the same three stones. Miss Wu marks a line inside the basin. Each test starts with water up to that line.

Ronan folds thick paper into a shallow tray. Mei holds one side. Ronan presses the corner flat. Leo watches another group make a long narrow shape.

“Ours should be longer,” Leo says.

“It is already folded.”

“We can unfold it.”

Mei puts down her hands. “Which one are we trying first?”

Ronan looks at their paper. He folded one part too hard. A dark line runs across that part.

“This one. Then the long one.”

Their tray floats. Ronan puts one stone in the middle. The paper dips but stays up. Leo reaches for the second stone.

“Wait,” Mei says. “I need to draw the first.”

“You draw fast.”

“Not that fast.”

Miss Wu is at another table. She helps the children mop up spilled water. She is busy with them. Ronan and his friends need to talk by themselves.

Ronan holds the second stone above the tray. He wants to know the next result. Mei has only drawn the first line.

“How about you watch this time,” he says, “and draw all three after?”

“The tests can be different. I need to see each one.”

He lowers the stone to the table.

They decide to make one small mark for each stone first. The pictures can come later. Mei draws a box with a one in it.

The second stone goes beside the first. The tray tilts. Leo moves it towards the middle with one finger. Water comes over the fold.

“Did that count?” Ronan asks.

Mei looks annoyed. “You moved it.”

“I was helping.”

Now the paper is soaked. It will not make the same test again.

They write about the test and Leo's finger. Their page needs all the facts. Leo's finger helped to hold the boat up. Leo touched it, and that changed the test. Must they start over? Ronan looks at Miss Wu.

Instead she asks, “What do you need next time?”

“Dry paper,” Leo says.

“And no fingers in the boat,” Mei adds.

“And time to make the marks,” Ronan says.

Miss Wu gives them another sheet for the next lesson. She has no more time today. The basin must be empty before the class comes back from lunch.

At the next table, a child has a dry boat with three stones inside. Leo goes over to look. He comes back. “That boat is wider than ours.” Ronan draws a second shape beside the wet tray. They need to try that wider shape themselves. Then they can compare it with their first tray. Mei writes WIDER beside the shape. Their page has the result from the first tray. The word WIDER is their plan for the next tray.

The three children carry the wet tray to a dry plate. At the bottom of the page, Mei draws a large finger above two tiny stones. Leo writes MY FINGER beside it himself.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- lid＝盖子
- shallow＝浅的
- soaked＝湿透的
- count＝算数

额外情节词（不要求本章全部记住）：paste＝浆糊；tray＝浅盘；tilt＝倾斜。

## 读句提示

**What do you need next time?**

下次／你们需要／什么？用直接问句，不把what嵌在asks后。

## 理解问题

1. 这次测试为什么不能只记成“能装两颗石头”？
2. 三个人怎样调整观察和记录的速度？
